name: App Attest and Play Integrity
plain: Proves to a server that a request came from a genuine copy of the app on a genuine device.
meaning: Anti fraud tool with a privacy angle: it is a device level key, not a user id.

android.permission: INTERNET (normal); Play Integrity API with Play services
android.store_policy: Play: Integrity API quotas (10,000 calls per day default)
android.note: Verdicts for device, app and account licensing

ios.note: Key stays in the Secure Enclave; DeviceCheck stores 2 bits per device

limits.headline: Can prove its requests come from the real app on a genuine phone
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you sign in, pay, or send something the app protects
can: Get a signed statement that the app and device look genuine
Sign requests with a key held in the phone's secure chip (iPhone)
Check app license and device integrity (Android)
Reject requests from copies, emulators and tampered apps
cannot: See who you are or other apps on the phone
Pass on a rooted or modified device at the stronger levels
Prove the phone is completely safe
Keep a flag beyond the 2 bits DeviceCheck offers
limits.reach_label: Proof about the app and phone
limits.differs: iPhone uses App Attest and DeviceCheck. Android uses Play Integrity verdicts.

story.what_it_is: A server gets proof that a request came from the real app on a genuine phone.

marketing.name: App Attest
marketing.pitch: Apple lets servers confirm requests come from a genuine copy of the app on Apple hardware.

marketing.name: Play Integrity API
marketing.pitch: Google tells servers whether a device, app and account look real or risky.

story.for_you: You do not see it. It sits behind a sign up, a purchase or a score upload and quietly says 'this looks real'. If your phone is jailbroken or rooted, an app may stop working.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to block bots, cheats and cloned apps. It is a device level proof, not a person level ID, which helps with privacy. It still decides which phones are allowed and which are turned away.

use_cases.example: A game server checks that a match result came from the real game, not a modified copy.
A bank checks that a transfer request came from its real app before it moves any money.
A ticket seller blocks scripts that buy up concert seats by checking each purchase.
A social app slows fake account creation by asking new devices to prove they are real.
An ad platform removes fake installs by confirming the app and device were genuine.
An AI app protects its paid server by only answering the true app.

risks: Device key can act as an identifier
story.android_note: Android uses Play Integrity and gives a graded answer (basic, device, strong) about the device.
story.ios_note: iPhone uses App Attest, which is a hardware key per app install plus a signed statement from Apple.

technical_bounds: Server must verify; clients cannot trust local result
